A name of the package stands for the default alias's backend, and for email a property of the handler does (`django/core/cache/__init__.py`, `django/core/files/storage/__init__.py`, `django/tasks/__init__.py`, `django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler`).

The cache's handler and the tasks' keep what they make in an asgiref `Local`, as the database's handler does, so each thread has its own backend for an alias; unlike the database's, they leave `BaseConnectionHandler.thread_critical` false, so code that `sync_to_async` or `async_to_sync` runs in another thread uses its caller's ([Connections by alias: `DATABASES` and `ConnectionHandler`](connections/aliases.md)) (`django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler`).

At the end of every request `close_caches`, a receiver of `request_finished`, closes the cache backends that the thread has made, which of the backends Django ships only `PyMemcacheCache` acts on (`django/core/cache/__init__.py:close_caches`).
The storage handler keeps one instance for each alias in a dictionary of its own, shared by every thread (`django/core/files/storage/handler.py:StorageHandler.__getitem__`).
The mail handler keeps nothing: each lookup imports the backend's class and makes a new instance (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).

The settings that configured the single backend before it, `EMAIL_BACKEND`, `EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_PORT` and the like, are deprecated, as are `django.core.mail.get_connection` and the `connection` argument of the sending functions; until they are removed in Django 2028, `mailers["default"]` falls back to `EMAIL_BACKEND` in a project that does not define `MAILERS` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

The first request found nothing in the cache under `"sailings"`, called list_sailings, which sent the query, and stored the list; the second found it and sent nothing to the database (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.get_or_set`).
The cache stored the list under `":1:sailings"`, the key the code gave with the cache's prefix, empty here, and its version, 1, in front of it (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:default_key_func`).

`Signal.send` calls the receivers connected for that sender or for every sender, in the order they were connected, with the signal, the sender and the keyword arguments of the send, and returns each receiver with what it returned (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.send`).

A receiver is held by a weak reference unless it is connected with `weak=False`, so a function or a method that nothing else keeps alive drops out of the list by itself (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.connect`).

The base class makes the key a backend stores from the key the code gives, and reads the **timeout**, how long an entry is kept: when a call gives none, the `"TIMEOUT"` of the cache's settings, 300 seconds unless they say otherwise; for `None`, for ever (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.__init__`, `django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.get_backend_timeout`).

Beside them, `django/utils/cache.py` writes the headers that tell a browser or a proxy how long it may keep a response, and decides whether a request's preconditions let Django answer 304 Not Modified or 412 Precondition Failed instead of sending the response again ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](services/http-caching.md)) (`django/utils/cache.py:get_conditional_response`).

A `File` wraps a Python file object, or anything that reads like one, and gives it a name, a size and a way to be read in chunks; `ContentFile` makes one from bytes or a string held in memory ([Files: `File`, `ContentFile` and their helpers](services/files.md)) (`django/core/files/base.py:File`).

`Storage.save` asks the storage for a name that is free, which by default is the name given if it is free and fits the field, and otherwise that name with an underscore and seven random characters added before its extension, shortened where the field's length requires; it saves the content and returns the name it used, which is the name a `django.db.models.FileField` keeps in its column (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.save`).

It writes nothing until it is asked: `EmailMessage.message` builds a message object of the standard library's `email` package from the parts and headers the message holds, adding a `"Date"` and a `"Message-ID"` unless its headers give them ([Email messages: `EmailMessage` and `EmailMultiAlternatives`](services/email-messages.md)) (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`).

A task is checked against its backend as it is made, and `Task.enqueue` hands it and its arguments to the backend, which returns a `TaskResult`, through which the caller follows the task's status and, once it has succeeded, its return value (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.enqueue`).
Its two backends are for development and tests: `ImmediateBackend` runs the task inside `enqueue`, and `DummyBackend` keeps the result and never runs it (`docs/topics/tasks.txt`).
The tasks framework, `django.tasks`, is new (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

Each format, `"json"`, `"jsonl"`, `"xml"`, `"yaml"` and `"python"`, is a module with a `Serializer` and a `Deserializer` class, built on the classes of those names in `django/core/serializers/base.py` (`django/core/serializers/__init__.py:BUILTIN_SERIALIZERS`).

It counts the objects, with the list's `count` method where it has one that takes no argument, as a queryset does, and gives each page a slice, which on a queryset becomes a LIMIT and, past the first page, an OFFSET in its SQL ([Pagination: `Paginator` and `Page`](services/pagination.md)) (`django/core/paginator.py:Paginator.page`).
